props.text: Gateway administration without the Designer: schedules, rosters, users and holidays are live views over the gateway's real user source — the admin screens every project rebuilds, as drop-in components. The last tab shows config-as-data: a validated JSON document plus the brand accent used by the Overview KPI cards.

config.script:
# Reference persistence: rebuild a BasicScheduleModel from the flat mirror
	# and write it to the gateway, then bump refreshTick so the binding refetches
	# and the component's dirty badge clears against the saved data. A rename
	# (event.oldName present) adds the new name first, then removes the old, only
	# once the add has worked. These calls report a failure in the UIResponse they
	# return, they don't raise.
	from com.inductiveautomation.ignition.common.user.schedule import BasicScheduleModel
	s = event.schedule
	name = unicode(s.name)
	old = getattr(event, 'oldName', None)
	# AUTHORIZE FIRST: the flags only hide UI, and a crafted client can send this event
	# with any payload. See the adminAuth project library.
	# Whether this creates is worked out from the gateway, not from event.isNew.
	names = [unicode(n) for n in system.user.getScheduleNames()]
	exists = name in names
	renaming = bool(old) and unicode(old) != name and unicode(old) in names
	creating = not exists and not renaming
	refused = adminAuth.refusal(self, ['editable', 'allowCreate'] if creating else ['editable'])
	if refused:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave REFUSED: ' + refused
		return
	# The create form is asking for a new schedule: don't overwrite one that has this name.
	# A rename onto another schedule would remove the old name with only config.editable,
	# which is a delete that gets around config.allowDelete.
	# A rename onto an UNUSED name still removes the old name with only config.editable, even with
	# config.allowCreate and config.allowDelete off. Tighten this if that doesn't suit your project.
	if exists and (renaming or bool(event.isNew)):
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave REFUSED: a schedule named "' + name + '" already exists'
		return
	# The manager checks names only in the browser, and the gateway stores an empty name, one
	# with a line break, and '..'. Checked only for a new name, so existing records stay editable.
	if creating or renaming:
		bad = adminAuth.nameProblem(name)
		if bad:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave REFUSED: ' + bad
			return
	m = BasicScheduleModel()
	m.name = name
	m.description = unicode(s.description)
	m.observeHolidays = bool(s.observeHolidays)
	m.allDays = bool(s.allDays)
	for day in ['monday', 'tuesday', 'wednesday', 'thursday', 'friday', 'saturday', 'sunday']:
		setattr(m, day, bool(s[day]))
		setattr(m, day + 'Time', unicode(s[day + 'Time']))
	def add(model):
		try:
			return system.user.addSchedule(model)
		except TypeError:
			return system.user.addSchedule(name, model)
	try:
		if renaming:
			action = 'renamed "' + unicode(old) + '" -> "' + name + '"'
			resp = add(m)
			if not list(resp.getErrors()):
				resp = system.user.removeSchedule(unicode(old))
		elif creating:
			action = 'created "' + name + '" (isNew=' + unicode(bool(event.isNew)) + ')'
			resp = add(m)
		else:
			action = 'persisted "' + name + '"'
			resp = system.user.editSchedule(name, m)
		errs = [unicode(x) for x in resp.getErrors()]
		if errs:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave ERRORS: ' + '; '.join(errs)
		else:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave ' + action
	except Exception as e:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onScheduleSave FAILED: ' + unicode(e)
	self.view.custom.refreshTick = self.view.custom.refreshTick + 1

transforms.code:
# The gateway's real rosters, plus a synthetic 'Demo Escalation' shown
	# until a save persists it for real (then the gateway copy wins).
	d = system.roster.getRosters()
	out = []
	for k in sorted(d.keys()):
		try:
			out.append({'name': str(k), 'users': [str(u) for u in d[k]]})
		except Exception:
			pass
	# Demo convenience: show the synthetic escalation when the gateway has no
	# (or only an EMPTY) 'Demo Escalation' — a save then persists it for real.
	demo = [r for r in out if r['name'] == 'Demo Escalation']
	if not demo:
		out.append({'name': 'Demo Escalation', 'users': ['jdoe', 'mvermeer', 'admin']})
	elif not demo[0]['users']:
		demo[0]['users'] = ['jdoe', 'mvermeer', 'admin']
	return out

# The 'default' user source as the picker directory. First ensure three demo
	# users exist (idempotent; kpatel deliberately has NO contact info so the
	# roster rows can show the warning) — a dev-gateway convenience, remove for
	# production bindings. NOTE: bare except on purpose — Jython's 'except
	# Exception' does not catch Java exceptions from system.user.
	import sys
	log = system.util.getLogger('RosterDemo')
	SRC = 'default'
	# DEMO ONLY, NEVER COPY THIS SEEDING: a binding runs for any session that opens the
	# view, with no login and no check, so this creates accounts with a known password for anyone.
	# A real binding only reads: delete ensure() and the calls to it.
	def ensure(username, first, last, contacts):
		try:
			if system.user.getUser(SRC, username) is None:
				u = system.user.getNewUser(SRC, username)
				u.set('firstname', first)
				u.set('lastname', last)
				u.set('password', 'Demo-1234!')
				for t, v in contacts:
					u.addContactInfo(t, v)
				resp = system.user.addUser(SRC, u)
				for err in resp.getErrors():
					log.warn('addUser(' + username + '): ' + str(err))
		except:
			log.warn('ensure(' + username + ') failed: ' + str(sys.exc_info()[1]))
	ensure('jdoe', 'Jane', 'Doe', [('email', 'jane.doe@example.com')])
	ensure('mvermeer', 'Mia', 'Vermeer', [('email', 'mia@example.com'), ('sms', '+31600000001')])
	ensure('kpatel', 'Kiran', 'Patel', [])
	out = []
	for u in system.user.getUsers(SRC):
		try:
			ci = []
			for c in u.contactInfo:
				ci.append({'contactType': str(c.contactType), 'value': str(c.value)})
			out.append({'username': str(u.get('username') or ''), 'firstName': str(u.get('firstname') or ''), 'lastName': str(u.get('lastname') or ''), 'contactInfo': ci})
		except:
			log.warn('map user failed: ' + str(sys.exc_info()[1]))
	return out

# Reference persistence: system.roster is append-only, so the full desired
	# order is rewritten wholesale — create if new, clear, then append in order.
	# addUsers/removeUsers take USER OBJECTS (not username strings): resolve
	# each username against the user source first. Bare except on purpose —
	# Jython's 'except Exception' does not catch Java exceptions.
	import sys
	name = unicode(event.name)
	wanted = [unicode(u) for u in event.users]
	# AUTHORIZE FIRST: the flags only hide UI, and a crafted client can send this event
	# with any payload. See the adminAuth project library.
	# Whether this creates is worked out from the gateway, not from event.isNew.
	creating = name not in [unicode(n) for n in system.roster.getRosterNames()]
	refused = adminAuth.refusal(self, ['editable', 'allowCreate'] if creating else ['editable'])
	if refused:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterSave REFUSED: ' + refused
		return
	# The create form is asking for a new roster: don't overwrite one that has this name.
	if bool(event.isNew) and not creating:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterSave REFUSED: a roster named "' + name + '" already exists'
		return
	# The manager checks names only in the browser, and the gateway stores an empty name, one
	# with a line break, and '..'. Checked only for a new name, so existing records stay editable.
	if creating:
		bad = adminAuth.nameProblem(name)
		if bad:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterSave REFUSED: ' + bad
			return
	try:
		if creating:
			system.roster.createRoster(name, 'Created from RosterDemo')
		current = system.roster.getUsers(name)
		if current:
			system.roster.removeUsers(name, current)
		objs = []
		missing = []
		for uname in wanted:
			u = system.user.getUser('default', uname)
			if u is None:
				missing.append(uname)
			else:
				objs.append(u)
		if objs:
			system.roster.addUsers(name, objs)
		msg = 'onRosterSave persisted "' + name + '" (' + unicode(len(objs)) + ' users, isNew=' + unicode(bool(event.isNew)) + ')'
		if missing:
			msg = msg + u' — skipped unknown: ' + ','.join(missing)
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = msg
	except:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterSave FAILED: ' + unicode(sys.exc_info()[1])
	self.view.custom.refreshTick = self.view.custom.refreshTick + 1

# AUTHORIZE FIRST: the flags only hide UI, and a crafted client can send this event
	# with any payload. See the adminAuth project library.
	refused = adminAuth.refusal(self, ['editable', 'allowDelete'])
	if refused:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterDelete REFUSED: ' + refused
		return
	import sys
	try:
		system.roster.deleteRoster(unicode(event.name))
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterDelete removed "' + unicode(event.name) + '"'
	except:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onRosterDelete FAILED: ' + unicode(sys.exc_info()[1])
	self.view.custom.refreshTick = self.view.custom.refreshTick + 1

# Reference persistence: rebuild a HolidayModel and write it back —
	# addHoliday when new, else editHoliday under the OLD name on a rename.
	import sys
	from com.inductiveautomation.ignition.common.user.schedule import HolidayModel
	s = event.holiday
	name = unicode(s.name)
	# AUTHORIZE FIRST: the flags only hide UI, and a crafted client can send this event
	# with any payload. See the adminAuth project library.
	# Whether this creates is worked out from the gateway, not from event.isNew.
	old = None
	try:
		old = event.oldName
	except:
		old = None
	names = [unicode(n) for n in system.user.getHolidayNames()]
	exists = name in names
	renaming = bool(old) and unicode(old) != name and unicode(old) in names
	creating = not exists and not renaming
	refused = adminAuth.refusal(self, ['editable', 'allowCreate'] if creating else ['editable'])
	if refused:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave REFUSED: ' + refused
		return
	# The create form is asking for a new holiday: don't overwrite one that has this name.
	if bool(event.isNew) and exists:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave REFUSED: a holiday named "' + name + '" already exists'
		return
	# The manager checks names only in the browser, and the gateway stores an empty name, one
	# with a line break, and '..'. Checked only for a new name, so existing records stay editable.
	if creating or renaming:
		bad = adminAuth.nameProblem(name)
		if bad:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave REFUSED: ' + bad
			return
	try:
		d = system.date.parse(unicode(s.date), 'yyyy-MM-dd')
		try:
			m = HolidayModel(name, d, bool(s.repeatAnnually))
		except:
			m = HolidayModel()
			m.name = name
			m.date = d
			m.repeatAnnually = bool(s.repeatAnnually)
		if creating:
			resp = system.user.addHoliday(m)
			action = 'created "' + name + '"'
		elif renaming:
			# The gateway refuses a rename onto an existing holiday and keeps both.
			resp = system.user.editHoliday(unicode(old), m)
			action = 'renamed "' + unicode(old) + '" -> "' + name + '"'
		else:
			resp = system.user.editHoliday(name, m)
			action = 'persisted "' + name + '"'
		errs = [unicode(x) for x in resp.getErrors()]
		if errs:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave ERRORS: ' + '; '.join(errs)
		else:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave ' + action
	except:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidaySave FAILED: ' + unicode(sys.exc_info()[1])
	self.view.custom.refreshTick = self.view.custom.refreshTick + 1

# AUTHORIZE FIRST: the flags only hide UI, and a crafted client can send this event
	# with any payload. See the adminAuth project library.
	refused = adminAuth.refusal(self, ['editable', 'allowDelete'])
	if refused:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidayDelete REFUSED: ' + refused
		return
	import sys
	try:
		resp = system.user.removeHoliday(unicode(event.name))
		errs = [unicode(x) for x in resp.getErrors()]
		if errs:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidayDelete ERRORS: ' + '; '.join(errs)
		else:
			self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidayDelete removed "' + unicode(event.name) + '"'
	except:
		self.view.custom.lastEvent = 'onHolidayDelete FAILED: ' + unicode(sys.exc_info()[1])
	self.view.custom.refreshTick = self.view.custom.refreshTick + 1
